summary: This report compares how cities worldwide modified transit service during planned events and emergencies after September 1, 2023. It covers proactive preparation for parades and festivities, rapid responses to earthquakes, power outages, storms and wildfires, and the roles of technology and human presence. It concludes that responsiveness, communication and collaboration are the key competencies, and that cities can learn from each other's protocols.
one_line: A comparative report on how global cities adapted and communicated transit service changes during planned events and emergencies after September 2023.
key_facts: On December 5, 2023, Transport for London prepared for the annual Christmas Parade with additional services, real-time updates via app and social media, and updated posters and digital signage; Simon Fletcher, Communications Manager, outlined the strategy.

For the Thanksgiving Day Parade on November 21, 2023, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority in New York deployed more staff, rerouted buses and adjusted subway services, coordinating with the NYPD according to spokesperson Naomi Rodriguez.

For the Emperor's Birthday on December 23, 2023, Tokyo Metro increased frequency on popular lines and placed bilingual staff at strategic locations; spokesman Hideki Sato stressed communication clarity.

After an earthquake hit Mexico City on September 17, 2023, the Metro System was temporarily suspended; Head of Operations Luis Ramírez said safety was the priority, and service was restored gradually starting with less affected areas.

During a power outage in Mumbai on October 2, 2023, Central Railway General Manager Sanjay Singh said backup power was deployed at critical junctions and emergency protocols were activated to safely disembark passengers.
During Typhoon Lan on October 29, 2023, Seoul used an intelligent traffic system that adjusted traffic signals and rerouted buses away from waterlogged areas, as noted by city official Min-jun Kim.

In Rome on November 12, 2023, a subway strike coincided with a major football match; authorities used informal negotiation to secure a temporary suspension of the strike, according to spokesperson Francesca Rinaldi.

During the San Francisco Bay Area wildfire on September 25, 2023, agencies sent push notifications via mobile apps and used satellite data to reroute buses away from smoke-affected areas; Operations Director Michael Chen called technology decisive for rider safety.

In Singapore during the Southeast Asian Games, AI and crowd-sourced data were used to project passenger flow; Lena Chua, Chief Information Officer at Land Transport Authority, said predictions allowed anticipatory scaling of services.

During the Paris Metro strike on October 15, 2023, station managers with handheld devices gave on-the-spot rerouting advice; Jean-Luc Martín of Customer Service stressed maintaining a human connection.
During the Toronto citywide blackout on November 4, 2023, volunteers helped transit staff manage passenger flow in dark stations; lead volunteer Olivia Johnson said human presence was reassuring.
The report identifies responsiveness, communication and collaboration as the core competencies for transit management during crises, shaped by cultural context.
